name: BACH_0069
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (80%)** · Ambiguous: Normal vs Benign · Careful review
Invasive probability is under 1%, but Normal is also in the 90% set [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 80%, Normal 18% | Benign leads; Normal plausible |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign | Two classes inseparable |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.955 / 94th percentile | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 Benign [F5] | Mostly Normal neighbors |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↓ invasive · Scarce here, lowering the concept model's invasive association · Validated [F3]
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 3, 10) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; text-only score, caption check inconsistent · Validated
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 1, 8, 11) · context · Above typical; descriptive only, spot check 8/20 · Weak [F2]
- **Neoplastic nuclei density** (regions 5, 6, 11) · context · 1,385 per mm², about 86th percentile; sampled regions only · Measured
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 5, 6) · ↑ invasive · Small positive term; spot check 3/20 · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions lowers the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60): faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007): not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules (0/20) and necrosis (3/20) are unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Benign and Normal are inseparable here; neighbors are mostly Normal.
- Only 3 of 12 regions were segmented, yet they show many neoplastic nuclei (up to 75, region 6).

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 5, 6, 11:** Judge whether the many neoplastic-labelled nuclei are truly atypical, or benign epithelium.
2. **Region 3:** Check for stromal invasion; the model scores it scarce.
3. **Regions 8, 1:** Verify lobules and TILs yourself; spot checks were poor (0/20, 8/20).
